title: Repair CSV column type inference
instructions:
Fix two bugs in `csv_sniffer.py`: blank cells currently pollute inferred types, and mixed integer/decimal columns fail to widen to float. Preserve the API:
- `sniff_column(values) -> str` consumes an iterable of strings. Strip each cell; ignore blank cells. Return `"unknown"` when none remain. Otherwise return `"bool"` if all are case-insensitive `true`/`false`, `"int"` if all match `[+-]?[0-9]+`, `"float"` if all are numeric and at least one is not an integer, or `"str"` otherwise. Numeric grammar is `[+-]?(?:[0-9]+(?:\.[0-9]*)?|\.[0-9]+)(?:[eE][+-]?[0-9]+)?`. This is lexical inference, with no conversion or range check. `NaN`, `inf`, underscores and boolean/numeric mixtures are strings.
- `sniff_csv(text) -> dict[str, str]`: parse standard comma CSV with Python's `csv.reader`; first row supplies exact, unstripped column names. Infer each column with `sniff_column`. Empty input returns `{}`; header-only columns are `unknown`. Ignore completely empty data rows (`[]`), but not rows containing blank cells. Raise `ValueError` for an empty header row, whitespace-only header names, duplicate exact names, or any nonempty data row with the wrong number of cells. Quoted commas and quoted newlines are supported. Inputs use valid CSV quoting.

## Files
- `csv_sniffer.py`
